Documentation

Unit

The Kyū (Q) unit: a precision measurement system for scalable, accessible design with pixel-level control.

The Kyū (Q) Unit

At the heart of unit.gl is the Kyū (級, Japanese for "grade" or "level"), a micro-unit that provides pixel-level precision while remaining scalable and accessible.

1Q = 0.0625rem = 1/16rem ≈ 1px (at 16px base font size)

The Q unit bridges the gap between pixel-perfect design and responsive, accessible layouts:

Context 1Q Equals Use Case
Digital (16px base) 1px Screen layouts, web interfaces
Digital (scaled) Scales with rem Accessible, user-preference aware
Print 0.25mm Physical media, typography

Why REM-based?

Using rem ensures your layouts respect user font size preferences, making your designs accessible by default.

The q() Function

The q() function is your primary tool for applying Q units:

@use "unit.gl" as *;

// Basic usage
.element {
  padding: q(16); // 1rem (16 × 0.0625rem)
  margin: q(8); // 0.5rem
  gap: q(24); // 1.5rem
  border-width: q(1); // 0.0625rem (≈1px)
}

// Negative values
.pull-up {
  margin-top: q(-8); // -0.5rem
}

// Calculations
.calculated {
  width: calc(100% - q(32));
}

Unit Conversion

Understanding how Q units convert to other measurements helps with design decisions:

Q Value REM PX (16px base) MM Common Use
q(1) 0.0625rem 1px 0.25mm Borders, very fine details
q(4) 0.25rem 4px 1mm Small gaps, micro spacing
q(8) 0.5rem 8px 2mm Base spacing unit
q(16) 1rem 16px 4mm Standard spacing (1rem)
q(24) 1.5rem 24px 6mm Medium spacing
q(32) 2rem 32px 8mm Large spacing
q(64) 4rem 64px 16mm Section spacing
q(128) 8rem 128px 32mm Major sections

Real-World Examples

Button Spacing

A typical button with consistent spacing:

.button {
  padding: q(8) q(16); // 4px 8px padding
  border-radius: q(4); // 1mm rounded corners
  font-size: q(14); // Text sizing
  gap: q(8); // Space between icon and text
}

Card Component

A card with proper spacing hierarchy:

.card {
  padding: q(24); // 1.5rem inner padding
  border-radius: q(8); // 2mm rounded corners
  box-shadow: 0 q(1) q(3) rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);
  margin-bottom: q(16); // Space between cards
}

.card__title {
  margin-bottom: q(8); // Title spacing
}

.card__description {
  margin-bottom: q(12); // Description spacing
}

Grid Layout

Consistent grid gaps using Q units:

.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
  gap: q(16); // 8px gaps between items
  padding: q(24); // Container padding
}

Accessibility & Responsive Scaling

One of the key advantages of Q units is that they respect user preferences and scale across different devices: 

// Q units automatically scale with the html font-size
// User sets 18px font size: q(16) becomes 1.125rem (18px)
// User sets 14px font size: q(16) becomes 0.875rem (14px)

// Your CSS stays the same
.component {
  padding: q(16); // Always 1rem, but scales with user preference
}

Browser Zoom & User Preferences

REM-based units respect browser zoom levels and user font-size preferences, making your designs accessible to users who need larger text.

Why Q Units?

Comparing different measurement approaches:

Approach Precision Accessible Consistent Scalable
Fixed PX ✓ Precise ✗ Ignores preferences ✗ Varies by design ✗ Fixed size
REM ✗ Limited precision ✓ Respects preferences ✗ Arbitrary values ✓ Scales automatically
Percentages ✗ Context-dependent ~ Sometimes ✗ Hard to control ✓ Responsive
Q Units ✓ Pixel-level precision ✓ Respects user font size ✓ Constrained & consistent ✓ Scales with design

Common Patterns Using Q Units

Spacing Scale

Build consistent spacing by using multiples of q(8):

@use "unit.gl" as *;

$space-xs: q(4);   // 0.25rem
$space-sm: q(8);   // 0.5rem
$space-md: q(16);  // 1rem
$space-lg: q(24);  // 1.5rem
$space-xl: q(32);  // 2rem
$space-2xl: q(48); // 3rem

// Usage
.component {
  padding: $space-md;
  margin-bottom: $space-lg;
  gap: $space-sm;
}

Typography Scale

Use Q units for consistent typography:

body {
  font-size: q(14); // Base size
  line-height: q(24); // 1.7 ratio
}

h1 { font-size: q(32); line-height: q(40); }
h2 { font-size: q(24); line-height: q(32); }
h3 { font-size: q(20); line-height: q(28); }
h4 { font-size: q(16); line-height: q(24); }

caption { font-size: q(12); }

Border & Radius

Control visual elements precisely:

// Border widths
$border-thin: q(1);
$border-default: q(2);
$border-thick: q(3);

// Border radius
$radius-sm: q(2);   // Subtle
$radius-md: q(4);   // Default
$radius-lg: q(8);   // Rounded
$radius-pill: q(128); // Full rounded
